claims.statement: If a physical 2x2 principal block B of a real symmetric quadratic-form matrix is definite, then for independent coordinate densities bounded by one the quadratic form has density at most pi/sqrt(|det B|).
claims.scope: All dimensions, arbitrary outside couplings and eigenvalues, positive or negative definite B.

claims.statement: For every n a power of two there is a matrix with eigenvalues 1,1,-1,0,...,0 and no definite physical 2x2 principal block.
claims.consequence: A fixed physical-pair conditioning proof is not forced by the target spectral hypothesis.

claims.statement: Three eigenvalues of magnitude at least one force a physical definite 2x2 principal block with dimension-free determinant lower bound.
claims.refutation: The Hadamard family has every physical pair determinant nonpositive.

dependencies.used_result: Same-sign diagonal pi lemma and pointwise-decay correction.
Rotated product-measure coupling identified as the open crux; duplicate diagonal/L3 work not republished.
